sources.title: RFC 7946: The GeoJSON Format
sources.publisher: IETF (Butler, Daly, Doyle, Gillies, Hagen, Schaub)

capture.delivered_note: first 32768 bytes delivered; covers sections 1 through 9, which include all locators cited

exact_locators: Section 3.1.1 Position: 'The first two elements are longitude and latitude, or easting and northing, precisely in that order'
Section 3.1.6 Polygon: right-hand rule; 'parsers SHOULD NOT reject Polygons that do not follow the right-hand rule'
Section 3.1.9 Antimeridian Cutting: geometry crossing the antimeridian 'SHOULD be represented by cutting it in two'
Section 3.1.10 Uncertainty and Precision: digit count 'MUST NOT be interpreted as an indication' of uncertainty
Section 3.2 Feature: unlocated Feature uses 'geometry': null
Section 4 Coordinate Reference System: WGS 84 only; alternative CRS support removed due to interoperability issues; processors not expected to have CRS databases or network access
Section 5.2 The Antimeridian: bbox across antimeridian has northeast-corner longitude less than southwest corner
Section 5.3 The Poles: 'MUST NOT use latitude values greater than 90 or less than -90'
sources.applicability: Defines the export/interchange coordinate semantics, antimeridian and incomplete-coordinate handling, and winding tolerance policy used in the proposal.

exact_locators: Section 3.1: first column is 64-bit signed integer; coordinate columns stored as 32-bit floating point ('rtree') or 32-bit integers ('rtree_i32'); non-conforming values silently converted
Section 3.4 Roundoff Error: bounds rounded outward; contained-within queries should expand boxes slightly (0.000012%)

Section 7.2 (TOC): integrity check using the rtreecheck() SQL function
sources.applicability: Basis of the spatial-index design, viewport query policy, bulk-operation pattern, and the index-is-a-filter principle (Precedent A).

sources.title: PROJ 9.9.0 FAQ
exact_locators: Section 'Why is the axis ordering in PROJ not consistent?': PROJ respects authority-defined axis order per ISO 19111; 'Before version 6, PROJ did not respect the standard either'; geodetic CRSs typically expect latitude/longitude while internally PROJ expects longitude/latitude; projinfo EPSG:4326 WKT2 shows AXIS latitude ORDER[1] then longitude ORDER[2]

Section 'What is the best format for describing coordinate reference systems?': WKT or SRIDs preferred; 'Conversions between WKT and PROJ strings will in most cases cause a loss of information, potentially leading to erroneous transformations'; WKT2 preferred
Section 'Can I transform from abc to xyz?': projinfo -s EPSG:25832 -t EPSG:4093 -o PROJ lists candidate operations with PROJ pipeline strings
Section 'Why am I getting the error Cannot find proj.db?': proj.db is a resource file; located via PROJ_DATA env var (PROJ_LIB before PROJ 9.1), then built-in resource dir, then current directory
sources.applicability: Basis of the axis-order contract, WKT2 storage choice, import-time transform validation, and proj.db pinning design (Precedent B).

Section 'How to credit OpenStreetMap': must display attribution notice and make clear data is available under ODbL

Section 'Additional services': 'Although OpenStreetMap is open data, we cannot provide a free-of-charge map API or map tiles for third-parties', linking API/Tile/Nominatim usage policies at operations.osmfoundation.org

sources.title: Syncthing documentation: Understanding Synchronization
sources.version_pin: docs footer 'Written for v2.1.0' (site version v2.1.0-24-g1f79d9e)
exact_locators: Section 'Conflicting Changes': modified-on-two-devices conflict renames one copy to '<filename>.sync-conflict-<date>-<time>-<modifiedBy>.<ext>'; older mtime loses; ties by device-ID bits; modification-vs-deletion can yield a conflict copy; conflict files propagate between devices
Section 'Temporary Files': never writes directly to destination; temp copy then move into place; leftover temp files kept up to a day
sources.applicability: Precedent C: explicit, visible, propagating conflict artifacts and atomic write pattern adopted by the merge/recovery design.
